title: ESXi Host with Isolated Private Network
summary: A bare-metal ESXi host separates a public vSwitch from a private one; a dual-NIC gateway VM bridges them for AD, brokers and session hosts.

nodes.label: Remote Users
nodes.detail: Connect to the published public address using a remote desktop client.

nodes.label: ESXi Host
nodes.detail: Type-1 hypervisor installed directly on hardware. Allocates CPU, memory, storage and virtual networks to VMs.

nodes.label: vSwitch0
nodes.detail: Virtual switch with a physical uplink NIC. Only the gateway VM's public interface attaches here.

nodes.label: Gateway VM
nodes.detail: One NIC on vSwitch0, one on vSwitch1. Routes and filters traffic, and publishes selected ports inward.

nodes.label: vSwitch1
nodes.detail: Internal-only switch with no physical uplink, so VMs on it are unreachable from outside except via the gateway.

nodes.label: Domain Controller
nodes.detail: Provides authentication, name resolution and addresses for all private VMs.

nodes.label: Connection Broker
nodes.detail: Authenticates users and directs each connection to an available session host.

nodes.label: Session Hosts
nodes.detail: Servers where user desktops or apps run, joined to the domain.

nodes.label: File Server
nodes.detail: Hosts shared folders and profile data on private storage, with permissions from AD groups.

steps.title: Hypervisor owns hardware
steps.text: ESXi runs on bare metal and defines two virtual switches for the VMs.

steps.title: Public traffic enters
steps.text: Users reach the gateway VM's public NIC through vSwitch0, the only switch with an uplink.

steps.title: Gateway bridges inward
steps.text: The dual-NIC gateway forwards permitted traffic to the private vSwitch1.

steps.title: Broker places the session
steps.text: The connection broker authenticates the user and assigns a session host.

steps.title: Domain services support it
steps.text: The domain controller supplies AD, DNS and DHCP, and the file server stores user data.
